summary: 1949 metal fire tower on Black Mountain, Chattahoochee National Forest, Union County, Georgia; NHLR-registered 2007. Fenced and locked; 2014 and 2018 visit reports.

facts.design: Metal tower with a 13 by 13 foot live-in cab and catwalk (NHLR)

access.note: Tower fenced with barbed wire; gate and cab door locked; no source says the public may climb it

visit.trail_note: The Appalachian Trail passes below the summit; the AT access detour is 0.4 mile with 400 feet of gain, per a hiker's history site. A 2014 visit report describes the access road as overgrown and steep, with about a mile on foot.

events.note: A hiker's history site says the lookout first appears on a 1938 map; this may mean an earlier structure. Unconfirmed.
NHLR and Georgia ForestWatch both give 1949; a paper sign on the fence names the Civilian Conservation Corps, which the Register does not repeat
Visit reports of January 19 and October 4, 2014: gate locked, tower unstaffed, radio repeater equipment installed
Visit report of November 25, 2018: windows removed and boarded, cab door locked and padlocked, structure appears sound

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1949 build date is kept, since the Register and Georgia ForestWatch agree. The 1938 map reference suggests an earlier lookout and is recorded as an unconfirmed event, not as a conflict that changes the build date.
The paper sign names the Civilian Conservation Corps; the Register names no builder. The story does not repeat the sign's attribution.

notes_for_editor: Best-documented of the three: the NHLR page has three visit reports (Jan 19 2014, Oct 4 2014, Nov 25 2018) covering staffing, locks, the road and condition. The 1949 build date matches NHLR and Georgia ForestWatch. The willhiteweb page is a hiker's history site; its paper-sign CCC attribution and 1938 map line are reported with attribution and not treated as established. The NHLR description calls the tower a '33' metal tower' with a CL-100 series cab; no height is recorded because the figure is unclear. The Oct 2014 'mile hike' and the 0.4-mile AT detour are different routes, not reconciled. A mountainquailpress.com result for Black Mountain describes a tower in California (San Jacinto Mountains) and was excluded. Access is recorded as closed because the tower is fenced and locked; no source says the public may climb it. The 2018 visit report is the latest condition evidence. Fact-check 2026-10-09: 'on the summit' removed from the lead (neither the Register nor ForestWatch says so; the hiker's site only mentions the summit in passing); the repeater sentence keeps the Register's 'it appears' hedge; 'accepted' changed to 'registered'; 'other users' replaced by the groups the hiker's site lists; the Register names no builder, which is a negative claim checked against the full page.
